extracted.intended_audience: applicant organizations (PD/PIs, Authorized Organization Representatives), NIH grants management and program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for NIH grant application disposition, pre-award (Just-in-Time) submissions, applicant and individual eligibility, Other Support disclosure, and cost/management system assessments that determine awardability. Applies to PD/PIs, AORs, and institutional grants offices preparing or responding to NIH pre-award requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council concurrence and second-level review
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members are asked to concur with the initial peer review for scientific and technical merit as judged by the SRG and to consider relevance to the IC’s programs and priorities. The Council may concur, decide not to recommend an application on program or policy considerations, or defer and refer back to the SRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council includes senior scientists and members of the public; with very limited exception an application may not be considered for funding unless it has received a favorable recommendation by both the SRG and the Council. Some second-level reviews for certain applications (e.g., Kirschstein NRSA) are conducted by senior IC staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council Review threshold and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members receive competing applications for PD/PIs that meet the threshold for Special Council Review: investigators who currently receive $2 million or more in total costs per year of NIH funding for Research Project Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council is asked to recommend consideration for applications that afford a unique opportunity to advance research highly promising and distinct from other funded projects from the PD/PI. This does not represent a cap on NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of incomplete/non-compliant/nonresponsive applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All incomplete applications, non-compliant applications, and applications determined to be nonresponsive to NOFO requirements will not be reviewed, consistent with 2 CFR 200.204 and 200.205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the NOFO remains open with subsequent submission dates, the applicant may resubmit a corrected or complete investigator-initiated application for the next review cycle. Resubmission timing rules apply (see resubmission window).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission window and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission (revised version) of an application may be submitted for an appropriate due date up to 37 months after the initial application due date, provided the NOFO allows resubmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application on the same topic proposed as a resubmission more than 37 months from the initial receipt date will not be accepted and must be formatted and submitted as a new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of summary statement and applicant follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: For complete, compliant, and responsive applications, following initial scientific peer review the summary statement will be available to the PD/PI and AORs with the Signing Official user role in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving summary statements should consult the NIH Next Steps page for guidance; applicants may contact the NIH Program Officer listed on the summary statement for advice beyond online information.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC Director final award authority and holding applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The IC Director or designee has authority to make final award decisions among applications receiving favorable initial review and Council recommendation. Applications not expected to be funded may be held for one or more additional cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision not to award or to award at a particular funding level is discretionary and not subject to appeal to any NIH or HHS official or board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in completing the pre-award process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that an IC may fund are reviewed for alignment with NIH funding principles, project budget, applicant management systems, applicant eligibility, and compliance with public policy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be asked for additional information (e.g., Other Support, IACUC approval) or to undertake activities (e.g., indirect cost rate negotiation). Such requests do not guarantee award. IC will determine awardability, need for specific award conditions, and funding level after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must continue to comply with eligibility and public policy requirements and maintain adequate management systems throughout the period of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-award reviews are repeated in a streamlined form for non-competing continuation awards, including assessment of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) procedures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses Just-in-Time procedures allowing certain application elements to be submitted later, after review, when the application is under consideration for funding; each NOFO will include specific guidance on use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants will be notified (primarily by e-mail) when JIT information is needed. This notification is not a Notice of Award and should not be construed as an indicator of possible funding. Submit JIT information only when requested, electronically via the eRA Commons JIT feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Just-in-Time elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard JIT elements include Other Support (active and pending) for senior/key personnel; certification of IRB approval for non-exempt human subjects research; verification of IACUC approval for live vertebrate animals; and evidence of completion of human subjects protection education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other program-specific information may also be requested. RFA timing and nature of required submissions will be specified in RFAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support: definition and inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other support includes all resources made available to a researcher in support of and/or related to all their research endeavors, regardless of monetary value or institutional base. This includes resources/financial support from foreign and domestic entities, financial support for lab personnel, and provision of high-value materials not freely available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional resources broadly available (core facilities/shared equipment) should not be included in Other Support but listed under Facilities and Other Resources. Consulting agreements where research is conducted as part of consulting and falls outside institutional appointment should be included. In-kind contributions (office/lab space, equipment, supplies, employees/students supported by outside sources) are included; provide reasonable estimates if dollar value or time is not readily ascertainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support exclusions (training awards, prizes, gifts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Support does not include training awards, prizes, or gifts. Gifts are resources provided where there is no expectation of anything in return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An item/service given with the expectation of an associated time commitment is not a gift and must be reported as an in-kind contribution under Other Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support certification and institutional internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PD/PI or other senior/key personnel must electronically sign their Other Support form prior to submission, certifying statements are true, complete, and accurate. NIH requires recipients to establish and maintain effective internal controls to ensure full disclosure of Other Support by senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal controls may include policies, trainings, and procedures; institutions must ensure timely disclosure to their institution as soon as Other Support information becomes known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documentation for foreign Other Support
rubrics_metrics.description: For Other Support submissions that include foreign activities and resources, recipients must submit copies of contracts, grants, or other agreements specific to senior/key personnel foreign appointments and/or employment as supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supporting documentation is not in English, recipients must provide translated copies. This requirement excludes personal service contracts or employment contracts for fellows supported by foreign entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC review of Other Support for effort and overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: IC scientific program and grants management staff will review Other Support to ensure sufficient levels of effort are committed and there is no scientific, budgetary, or commitment overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any identified overlap will be resolved by the IC with the applicant and PD/PI at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific overlap definition and prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific overlap occurs when (1) substantially the same research is proposed in more than one application or submitted to multiple funding sources, or (2) a specific research objective and the research design for accomplishing the objective are the same or closely related in two or more applications or awards, regardless of funding source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific overlap is not permitted and will be addressed before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary overlap definition and prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgetary overlap occurs when duplicate or equivalent budgetary items (e.g., equipment, salaries) are requested in an application but already provided by another source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary overlap is not permitted and will be resolved by the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment overlap definition and prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment overlap occurs when an individual’s time commitment exceeds 100 percent (i.e., 12 person-months), whether or not salary support is requested in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any overlap, including commitment >100 percent, is not permitted; the IC will resolve overlap with the applicant and PD/PI at award time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only necessary funds included in award
rubrics_metrics.description: Only funds necessary for the approved project are included in the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs review requested budgets and make determinations consistent with reasonable and allowable costs and program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign resources as non-monetary foreign component require approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any foreign resources that meet the definition of a non-monetary foreign component must have received appropriate prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is reviewed as part of pre-award consideration and Just-in-Time submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of IRB approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed project involves human subjects research, certification that all non-exempt human subjects research has been reviewed and approved by an appropriate IRB must be submitted; pending or expired approvals are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public Policy Requirements/Human Subjects for additional information and required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of IACUC approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed project involves live vertebrate animals, verification of the date of IACUC approval of the animal-use sections and any IACUC-imposed changes must be submitted; pending or out-of-date approvals are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public Policy Requirements/Animal Welfare for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protection education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed project involves human subjects research, certification that any person identified as senior/key personnel involved in human subjects research has completed an education program in the protection of human subjects must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public Policy Requirements/Human Subjects/Education in the Protection of Human Research Participants for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: hESC line identification in Just-in-Time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a project involves human embryonic stem cells and the applicant did not identify an hESC line from the NIH Registry in the application, the line(s) should be included in the Just-in-Time submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may request additional documentation related to hESCs during JIT; applicants should follow NIH Registry requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Data Sharing Institutional Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project involves research subject to the Genomic Data Sharing policy for generating human genomic data, investigators must submit an Institutional Certification (or in some cases a Provisional Institutional Certification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification forms and directions are on the NIH GDS Data Sharing website and must be submitted as a 'Genome Data Sharing Certification' file in the eRA Commons JIT module.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR foreign disclosure and funding agreement certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR competing applicants must submit the Required Disclosure of Foreign Affiliations or Relationships to Foreign Countries form; SBIR and STTR Funding Agreement Certifications must be provided upon request per supplemental instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms must be uploaded in the eRA Commons JIT module under specified file types; links to fillable forms are provided in the supplemental instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: My Bibliography report for training program renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewal applicants to research training programs, a My Bibliography Report of Publications arising from trainee work supported by the training grant will be collected in the Interim/Final Research Performance Progress Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of reporting/renewal requirements for training grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC may request other Just-in-Time or pre-award information
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH ICs may request additional JIT information on a case-by-case basis, such as revised budgets or changes to human subjects or vertebrate animals sections; required items must be submitted as 'Other Upload' in the eRA Commons JIT module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, changes must be submitted through the specified eRA Commons upload channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting revised Project Summary/Abstract/Specific Aims/Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: When requested as part of pre-award, PD/PIs and AOR should discuss potential scope changes with NIH PO and revise Project Summary/Abstract, Specific Aims, and/or Public Health Relevance as appropriate and e-mail a single Microsoft Word file with final versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All revised application information must be approved by an AOR. Use the NIH template with specific headings that must be included (include headers even if text is blank). Submit to the IC-designated e-mail address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant organization eRA Commons registration and eligibility checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicant organizations must complete one-time eRA Commons registration prior to submitting any application. NIH may make a preliminary assessment of organizational eligibility during registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To streamline registration, consider eligibility considerations: nature of research/business and fit with NIH mission; organizational responsibility for research; organization size; whether researchers are employed by the organization; physical location of proposed research; identification of an applicable NOFO; prior direct Federal funding. NIH may deny registration if organization not appropriate for a specific NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and documentation must identify authorized individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not accept forms or documentation bearing generic departmental signatures or electronic equivalents (e.g., Department of Sponsored Research). All forms must reflect the name of the individual with appropriate institutional authority to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOR's signature on the application certifies that the applicant is eligible to apply for and receive an award (e.g., small business status for SBIR/STTR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility limitations and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awards may be made only to eligible applicants; NIH may limit eligibility for certain programs or awards (e.g., foreign entities, small businesses). Determination of eligibility includes verification of applicant status and may require documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued funding depends on continued eligibility. NIH reserves the right to deny registration or award if statutory, regulatory, or published policy limitations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award made only to applicant with substantive role (no conduit recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not make an award to an applicant that does not have a substantive role in the project and would simply serve as a conduit for another entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s concern is making an award to a legal entity accountable for performance of the project and appropriate expenditure of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining eligibility of individuals (debarment, citizenship, visas)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant organization must select individuals with appropriate expertise. GMO will verify whether proposed PD/PI or senior/key personnel are debarred or suspended from Federal assistance programs. Generally, PD/PIs and personnel are not required to hold specific degrees or be U.S. citizens, but some programs have citizenship requirements stated in the NOFO; citizenship is required at time of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must ensure visa status allows individuals to remain long enough to be productive on the project; NIH does not assess visa types but may terminate a grant if visa will not allow sufficient stay. Institutions are expected to have consistently applied policies regardless of funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award monitoring of recipient and project status
rubrics_metrics.description: In the post-award phase, NIH monitors changes in recipient and project status to ensure they meet legal and programmatic requirements and will take actions necessary to protect the Federal government's interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring includes continued eligibility, compliance with public policy, and management system adequacy; enforcement actions may follow noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost analysis for detailed budgets and assessment of management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The GMO will ensure a cost analysis is performed on any application requiring a detailed budget, involving cost breakdowns, validating cost data, evaluating elements of cost, and examining data to determine necessity, reasonableness, and allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent of cost analysis depends on funding instrument/mechanism, project complexity, prior experience with applicant, and other factors. Applicable cost principles and allowable/unallowable costs are in the Cost Considerations chapter. The GMO will determine adequacy of financial and business management systems and may review audits; based on review results the GMO may require corrective action or impose specific award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of NIH funding based on reasonable and allowable costs and IC priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of NIH funding is based on reasonable and allowable costs consistent with sound cost management, considering IC priorities (e.g., program relevance), constraints on growth of average grant costs, and available funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs balance requested budgets with priorities and available appropriations when deciding funding levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Standard Terms of Award and incorporation of statutes and NIHGPS
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awards are subject to statutes, program regulations cited in the NoA, the NIHGPS (including addenda in effect at the budget period start), 2 CFR Part 200, and terms and conditions cited on the NoA or attachments. NIH implements Federalwide standard terms for research awards (NIH Standard Terms of Award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms and conditions in the NIHGPS supplement statutory/regulatory requirements; in case of conflict statutes/regulations govern. Recipients should request written clarification from the GMO if conflicts or questions arise, preferably before drawing funds.
